exposure: intrathecal 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine 12.5 mg combined with fentanyl 25 mcg
outcome: neonatal APGAR score (appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration)
frequency of side effects (nausea, vomiting, shivering)
cohort: Sixty ASA I and II patients scheduled for elective lower segment cesarean sections, giving birth to term gestation neonates, were included.
finding: In elective cesarean sections, 0.5% heavy Bupivacaine combined with 25 mcg of fentanyl is preferable to 0.5% heavy Bupivacaine alone, as it results in longer durations for two-segment regression and total sensory blocking, and a lower frequency of side effects, without affecting the neonatal APGAR score.
mod_finding: The study found that for lower segment cesarean sections, combining bupivacaine with fentanyl improved the duration of sensory block and reduced maternal side effects compared to bupivacaine alone, with no impact on newborn APGAR scores.
cross-section timing: During and immediately after elective cesarean section
